title: Avoiding Straight Tees on Horizontal Waste Lines
description: Using a standard straight tee in horizontal waste lines is a frequent mistake that leads to chronic clogs. Horizontal drainage relies on smooth directional transitions to move wastewater and solids without turbulence or resistance. Straight tees direct flow at a 90-degree angle, causing solids to impact the pipe wall, accumulate, and back up. Code requires directional fittings, such as a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep turn, for horizontal-to-horizontal waste transitions. Correct fitting selection maintains velocity and prevents solid waste buildup inside the drainage piping.
